examples.en: I often get compared to my older sister, and it upsets me.
The prices of the two companies can be compared at a glance.

examples.ko: 다른 사람과 비교되면 기분이 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't feel good when I'm compared with others.

examples.ko: 이 두 식당은 맛과 가격이 자주 비교되는 곳이에요.
examples.en: These two restaurants are often compared on taste and price.

examples.ko: 새 영화는 전편과 비교될 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: The new movie can't help being compared with the original.
Children really dislike being compared to their siblings.

explain: '비교하다'는 내가 견주는 것이고, '비교되다'는 견주어지는 쪽이에요. 'A가 B와 비교되다'처럼 '와/과'를 써요. 형제나 친구와 비교되는 일은 기분이 상하기 쉬워서, 한국에서는 '비교하지 마세요'라는 말을 자주 해요.

phrases.en: I don't like being compared with my older brother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 게 싫다'로 비교당하는 불편한 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-는 게 싫다' expresses the discomfort of being compared.

phrases.example: 이 가게는 늘 옆 가게와 비교돼요.
phrases.en: This shop is always compared with the shop next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '와/과'를 붙여 비교의 대상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '와/과' marks the thing being compared with.

phrases.example: 두 가게의 음식이 자꾸 서로 비교돼요.
phrases.en: The food at the two shops keeps getting compared with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서로'와 함께 두 대상이 함께 견주어진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '서로', it means two things are being weighed against each other.
phrases.en_equiv: to be compared with each other

explain_en: Passive: one thing is measured against another, often unfavorably. '비교하다' is you comparing; '비교되다' is being the one compared. The pattern is 'A가 B와 비교되다' with '와/과'. Being compared to a sibling or friend easily hurts feelings, so '비교하지 마세요' is a common thing to say in Korea.

en: to be referred to; to be consulted

examples.en: This material was referred to in the report.
Your opinions will be taken into account.
The book that was consulted is in the library.
This will be considered in the review.

examples.ko: 이 문서가 참고되고 있는지 확인해 주세요.
examples.en: Please check whether this document is being referred to.
The old records weren't consulted.

explain: 자료나 의견이 판단하거나 결정할 때 도움으로 쓰인다는 말이에요. 내가 볼 때는 '참고하다'를 써요. '참고로 말씀드리면'은 덧붙여 알려 줄 때 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: This book is a helpful reference for studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참고가 되다'는 도움이 된다는 뜻으로 '참고되다'와 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '참고가 되다' means it is helpful and is close to 참고되다.

phrases.en: The students' opinions were taken into account in the plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 참고되다'로 어디에 쓰였는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '~에 참고되다' tells where something was used as a reference.

phrases.example: 이 자료가 지금 보고서에 참고되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This material is being used as a reference for the report now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 참고 자료로 쓰이는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is being used as a reference right now.

explain_en: It means a source or opinion is used as an aid when judging or deciding. When you are the one consulting, the active verb is used. A related phrase, 'for your reference', is used to add extra information.

examples.en: Please mark the wrong problems with a cross.
The teacher put a cross on the wrong answer.
If it's right, make a circle. If it's wrong, make a cross.
Don't put a cross in this box.
There are so many crosses on my test paper that I'm upset.
A cross mark is also called an X mark.

explain: 동그라미(○)와 반대로 틀렸다는 표시를 말해요. '가위표를 하다/치다'처럼 써요. 같은 모양을 '엑스(X) 표시'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I marked the wrong answer with an X.
phrases.nuance_ko: '치다'는 줄이나 표시를 그을 때 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 치다 is the verb used for drawing a line or a mark.

phrases.en: I put an X mark on the wrong question.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가위표'와 같은 뜻으로, 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 가위표 and common in speech.

phrases.en: If it's right, I draw a circle, and if it's wrong, an X.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맞음과 틀림을 나란히 말할 때 두 낱말을 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two words are used together to talk about right and wrong.

explain_en: It is the opposite of a circle (○) and shows that an answer is wrong. You say '가위표를 하다/치다'. The same mark is also called an 'X 표시'.

examples.en: Our club is recruiting new members.
The company recruited new employees.
I saw a notice recruiting volunteers.
Until when do you plan to recruit participants?
I'll let you know as soon as we recruit students.
I was surprised that more people signed up than expected.

explain: 사람을 구하는 쪽이 '모집하다'를 쓰고, 들어가려는 쪽은 '지원하다'를 써요. 회사가 최종으로 뽑아서 일을 시키는 건 '채용하다'예요. 광고에는 '신입 사원 모집'처럼 '하다' 없이 붙여 써요.

phrases.en: Our store is recruiting part-time workers.
phrases.nuance_ko: '모집하다'의 해요체로, 사람을 구하는 쪽이 현재의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form of 모집하다, used by the side that is looking for people.

phrases.en: We are recruiting new members right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중'을 붙여 지금 모집이 진행되고 있다는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 중 shows that recruiting is going on right now.

phrases.example: 이번 달에는 신입 사원을 모집하지 않아요.
phrases.en: We are not recruiting new employees this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로, 지금은 사람을 구하지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used to say you are not looking for people now.

explain_en: Openly call for members, applicants or students (회원을 모집하다) The side looking for people uses 모집하다, and the side wanting to join uses '지원하다' (apply). When a company finally selects someone and hires them, that is '채용하다'. Ads drop 하다 and just say '신입 사원 모집'.

en: to return (a borrowed item); to give back

examples.ko: 저는 일주일에 한 번 도서관에 책을 반납해요.
examples.en: I return books to the library once a week.
I returned the umbrella I borrowed yesterday to my friend.
By when do I have to return this book?
If you return it late, you have to pay.
I returned the hotel key and left.

examples.ko: 반납하러 갔는데 도서관 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I went to return it, but the library was closed.

explain: 책, 열쇠, 우산, 렌터카처럼 '빌린 것'을 돌려줄 때 써요. 산 물건을 가게에 돌려주고 돈을 받는 건 '환불하다'예요. 빌린 돈을 돌려줄 때는 '반납하다'가 아니라 '갚다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 책을 다 읽으면 도서관에 반납해 주세요.
phrases.en: When you finish the book, please return it to the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빌려 간 사람에게 돌려 달라고 공손하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to give back what they borrowed.

phrases.en: Today is the day to return the book.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 날'을 붙여 돌려줘야 하는 날을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -는 날 to refer to the day something must be returned.

phrases.en: I'm sorry I returned the book late.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늦게'를 앞에 붙여 정해진 때보다 늦은 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 늦게 means returning after the due time.

explain_en: Library books, rented items, office equipment — returning on due date. Use it for things you borrowed: books, keys, umbrellas, rental cars. Taking a purchase back to a shop for your money is '환불하다'. For borrowed money, use '갚다', not '반납하다'.

t90.ax: I returned the hotel key and left.

en: to set; to set up; to arrange

examples.en: I set up the chairs in advance before a meeting.
Yesterday I set up my new computer.
We will set up the stage tomorrow morning.

examples.ko: 머리를 세팅하는 데 삼십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes thirty minutes to style my hair.
I set the seats and waited for the guests.
I set the alarm and woke up early.

explain: 컴퓨터 준비, 행사장 준비, 머리 모양 만들기에 모두 써요. 영어 setting에서 온 외래어라서 대화에서 많이 들리고, 글에서는 '준비하다'나 '설정하다'가 더 자연스러울 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 손님이 오기 전에 상을 세팅해 놓았어요.
phrases.en: I set the table before the guests came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 준비해 둔다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feel of preparing in advance.

phrases.en: Please prepare the meeting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '세팅하다'보다 글에서도 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in writing than 'seteinghada'.

phrases.en: I set the alarm on my phone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 앱의 기능을 맞출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when adjusting a device or app function.

explain_en: Loanword; arrange or prepare, e.g. a table or hair. It covers setting up a computer, preparing an event space, and styling hair. It is a loanword from English 'setting', common in speech; in writing '준비하다' or '설정하다' often sounds more natural.

t90.ax: I set the alarm and woke up early.

en: to write; to fill in; to draw up

examples.ko: 이 서류를 오늘 안에 작성해 주세요.
examples.en: Please fill out this form by the end of today.
I wrote my résumé last night.

examples.ko: 보고서를 작성하는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to write a report.
Write your name and address in this box.
I wrote the email and sent it right away.

examples.ko: 계획서를 작성할 때는 이 예시를 참고하세요.
examples.en: Use this example as a reference when you write the plan.

explain: 일기나 편지처럼 마음 가는 대로 쓰는 글은 '쓰다'이고, '작성하다'는 서류·보고서·이력서처럼 형식이 있는 문서에 어울려요. 은행이나 병원에서 종이를 주며 '작성해 주세요'라고 자주 말해요. 일상 대화에서 '일기를 작성했어요'라고 하면 조금 딱딱하게 들려요.

phrases.en: I fill out an application form at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '작성하다'보다 '쓰다'를 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, '쓰다' is used more than '작성하다'.

phrases.en: Please tell me how to write a résumé.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류를 쓰는 방식을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking how to write a document.

phrases.en: Please hand in the document you filled out at the counter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 다 쓴 문서를 앞에서 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a document that has already been written.

explain_en: Formal, for documents, reports and forms, filled in whole. For diaries or letters you simply say '쓰다'. 작성하다 suits documents with a set format, such as forms, reports and résumés. At a bank or hospital you will often hear '작성해 주세요' when they hand you a form. Saying '일기를 작성했어요' (a diary) in conversation would sound stiff.

gh: everyday write by hand; also use
enter details on a form; formal
notate or label in a writing system
write a book or article; formal

p.n: Works, but the replacement is plainer and less formal.

t90.ax: I wrote my résumé last night.

examples.en: I dried the wet clothes in the sun.
If you dry laundry in a dryer, it dries fast.
Mushrooms are dried and stored for a long time.
Dry your hair completely before you go out.
I like snacks made of dried fruit.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 공기를 건조시키는 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: This machine has a function that dries the air.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 보통 '말리다'를 써요. '건조시키다'는 기계, 식품, 공장 이야기처럼 딱딱한 설명에 어울려요. '날씨가 건조하다'는 형용사 '건조하다'라서 달라요.

phrases.example: 건조시킨 과일은 오래 보관할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Dried fruit can be stored for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 말려서 만든 것을 설명할 때 명사 앞에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe food that has been dried.

phrases.en: I slowly dried the leaves in the shade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 방법으로 말리는지 '천천히', '빨리' 같은 말과 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with words like '천천히' or '빨리' to say how something is dried.

phrases.example: 이 기계로 쌀을 빨리 건조시킬 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can dry rice quickly with this machine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 방법으로 말릴 수 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain that a machine or method can dry something.

explain_en: Technical, formal — deliberately dry something (햇볕에 건조시키다) In everyday talk, '말리다' is the usual word. '건조시키다' suits stiff explanations about machines, food, and factories. '날씨가 건조하다' uses the adjective '건조하다', which is a different word.

t90.ax: I like snacks made of dried fruit.

en: to mop; to wipe with a rag

examples.en: Every weekend I mop the living room floor with a cloth.
You need to sweep and then wipe the room to get rid of dust.
I scrubbed hard with a cloth, and the floor got clean.

examples.ko: 제가 걸레질할 테니까 청소기를 돌려 주세요.
examples.en: I'll wipe the floor, so please run the vacuum cleaner.

examples.ko: 부엌 바닥은 물걸레로 걸레질하면 잘 닦여요.
examples.en: The kitchen floor gets clean if you wipe it with a wet cloth.
Keep the windows open while you wipe the floor.

explain: 걸레로 바닥이나 가구를 닦는 일이에요. '걸레질을 하다'와 '걸레질하다'를 둘 다 써요. 보통 '쓸기·청소기'로 먼지를 치운 다음에 해요.

phrases.en: When I clean, I mop last.
phrases.nuance_ko: '걸레질하다'와 같은 뜻으로, '을 하다'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 걸레질하다, with 을 하다 added.

phrases.en: I wiped the desk with a cloth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇으로 닦는지 도구를 같이 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to mention the tool you wipe with.

phrases.en: I vacuumed and then wiped the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청소 순서를 말할 때 먼저 먼지를 치우고 나서 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the cleaning order: remove dust first, then wipe.

explain_en: It is wiping the floor or furniture with a cloth. Both '걸레질을 하다' and '걸레질하다' are used. It usually comes after removing dust by sweeping or vacuuming.

en: piece of wood; block of wood; chunk of wood

examples.en: The child is building a house with wooden blocks.
I gathered pieces of wood to make a fire.
A small piece of wood is rolling around on the floor.
I used a block of wood instead of a chair.
He carved a piece of wood with a knife and made a doll.
I put a piece of wood under the desk leg.

explain: '토막'은 잘라 낸 한 조각을 말해서, 나무토막은 잘려 있는 나무 조각이에요. 불 피울 때 쓰는 나무는 '장작'이라고 해요. 집 짓기 놀이를 하는 장난감 블록도 나무토막이라고 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I made a toy from a small piece of wood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크기를 말하는 '작은'과 자주 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 작은 to describe size.

phrases.en: The child stacked the wooden blocks high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 블록 놀이를 할 때 '쌓다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 쌓다 for block play.

phrases.en: The child made a tower out of wooden blocks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 말할 때 '으로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 으로 to say what something is made from.

explain_en: A thick chunk cut off, like a block (for toys) '토막' is a cut-off piece, so a 나무토막 is a piece of wood that has been cut. Wood used for a fire is called '장작'. Wooden toy blocks for building can also be called 나무토막.

t90.ax: I gathered pieces of wood to make a fire.

examples.en: Please put the leftover side dishes in the fridge compartment.
The fridge compartment door doesn't close properly.
I slowly thaw the meat from the freezer in the fridge compartment.
I lowered the temperature of the fridge compartment a little.

examples.ko: 우유는 냉장실 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The milk is on the top shelf of the fridge compartment.

examples.ko: 냉장실이 꽉 차서 더 못 넣어요.
examples.en: The fridge compartment is full, so I can't put in any more.

explain: 냉장고 안에서 얼리지 않고 차갑게 보관하는 칸을 말하고, 반대는 얼리는 '냉동실'이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '냉장고'라고 하는 경우가 많아요. 칸을 나눠서 말할 때 냉장실과 냉동실이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please put the milk in the fridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '냉장실' 대신 '냉장고'라고 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech people often say 냉장고 instead of 냉장실.

phrases.en: Please keep the fruit in the fridge section.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차갑게 보관할 칸을 정확히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to name the exact compartment for cold storage.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in the fridge section

phrases.en: Please close the fridge section door tightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 냉장실의 문을 열고 닫는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when talking about opening or closing the fridge section door.

explain_en: The cooling section inside, as opposed to the freezer. It is the part of the refrigerator that keeps food cold without freezing, and the opposite is the freezer, '냉동실'. In daily speech people often just say '냉장고'. You use 냉장실 and 냉동실 when separating the two compartments.

examples.en: I iron my shirts on Sunday evening.

examples.ko: 면 소재는 다림질하기 전에 물을 살짝 뿌려요.
examples.en: I spray cotton lightly with water before ironing it.
I ironed my suit the day before the interview.
I almost burned my hand while ironing.
The shirt I had ironed got wrinkled again right away.

examples.ko: 시간이 없어서 다림질하지 못하고 그냥 입었어요.
examples.en: I had no time to iron it, so I just wore it as it was.

explain: '옷을 다리다', '다리미질하다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 말해요. '옷을 다림질하다'처럼 목적어를 붙여 쓰고, 구김을 펴는 일이라 '구겨지다'와 짝으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I iron dress shirts on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다림질하다'와 같은 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 다림질하다.

phrases.en: I iron my clothes before going to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧고 일상적인 말투로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short, everyday way of saying it.

phrases.en: Please iron these pants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세탁소나 가족에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking a laundry shop or family member.

explain_en: Standard, much more common word for ironing clothes (와이셔츠 다림질) People also say '옷을 다리다' or '다리미질하다' with the same meaning. It takes an object like '옷을 다림질하다', and often appears alongside '구겨지다' (to get wrinkled).

t90.ax: I iron my shirts on Sunday evening.
